analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Nvidia in focus; Semis a dead cat bounce? Tencent & Baba previews; WISE food for thought; ASML customer wins; Indra (16 Nov 2026)
key_insights: SOX fell 3.4% on Friday and the sell-off spread to Asia on Monday: regional tech stocks dropped more than 5%, Samsung fell 4.5% and SK Hynix lost 8%.

Nvidia reports Tuesday. Interim CEO Colette Kress faces scrutiny over leadership uncertainty and export-control compliance. The FT, cited by Reuters, reports Jensen Huang is discussing a return, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has called for an external successor and a leadership shake-up.

The semiconductor debate has moved beyond Nvidia to the AI ecosystem's dependence on its funding capacity, multi-year pre-purchase commitments and supplier relationships. Near-term physical supply is not the concern (backlogs and TSMC allocations intact). The concern is whether new leadership keeps deploying the balance sheet at the same scale, given Nvidia's role as lender of last resort through capacity backstops, residual-value guarantees and equity stakes. 2028 is the key focus point for the pre-commitment model.

Tighter China controls, including a possible MATCH Act revival (more negative for ASML than ASM), and any Chinese retaliation are parallel risks. Spying-related allegations raise the odds of broader US/China measures that could pressure equipment names. Reliance on Chinese open models is a secondary vulnerability for some inference businesses.
Nebius's Q3 guide cut on power delays hurt sentiment around neocloud execution risk.

Positioning is cautious: tech led global net selling for the week, the US Info Tech long/short ratio fell to its lowest in the GS PB dataset going back to 2016, and flows shifted from long liquidation and de-grossing to a pickup in new shorts. The cash desk saw persistent NVDA supply from long-only holders, with money rotating into hyperscalers and other large-cap tech.
SPXXAI has outperformed SPX over the last year and was more resilient in last week's sell-off. NDX snapped a four-week losing streak, helped by semis.

GIR (Ronald) says tighter US limits on China's access to rented or remote computing power could constrain Chinese AI labs' ability to train the largest models, but AI applications and day-to-day use should stay resilient, increasingly on domestic chips. This points to a more separate Chinese AI ecosystem, and China's vertically integrated internet giants could be better placed than independent AI labs.

Nvidia earnings Tuesday night: sellside consensus is $108.8-109.3bn revenue and adjusted EPS of $2.47-2.49. The stock trades at 11x next-12-month earnings with a 14-day RSI of 24, the lowest since 2019. Investors want a clear revenue beat, gross margin at or above the 74% guide, and reassurance on roughly 70% FY2028 revenue growth.

Vera Rubin volume shipments could slip from year-end into 1H27 on HBM4 shortages per local press, leaving GB300 as this year's main product. Investors want evidence demand is supply-constrained rather than weakening, clarity on memory-cost pressure, and reassurance on strategy and the leadership transition. China restrictions, buybacks and AI financing commitments are also in focus.

Alibaba and Tencent are both down about 36% YTD with subdued investor engagement. GS expects Alibaba cloud growth to accelerate to 53% with margins improving to 12.5%, while Quick Commerce losses remain a drag. GS expects Tencent 3Q revenue +9% YoY on gaming, advertising and cloud, with AI investment weighing on margins. Tencent reports Wednesday and Alibaba Thursday.

GS sees an improving setup for China Internet into 2027: H-share Internet profit growth accelerating from -3% in 2026 to +18% in 2027, versus slowing earnings growth in Korea/Taiwan. Renewed KWEB/FXI inflows suggest positioning may be turning.

ASML reportedly has two new EUV customers, Taiwanese DRAM makers Nanya and Winbond. Nanya's Fab 5A gets equipment in Q1 2027, production by end-2027, 30,000 wafers/month by end-2028 and 50,000 by end-2030. Winbond expects its first EUV tool in about two years and plans EUV for its second-generation 14nm process in 2030.

WISE: ex-balance-sheet cash it trades on 13x P/E for a 20%+ growth business, with gross margin expanded by more than 20% despite price cuts. It has 2% market share versus Adyen at 6%. The desk calls it unloved and says it has solved a few regulatory issues.

Overloaded network equipment disrupted US air traffic control on Friday, grounding flights for more than four hours and causing nearly 10,000 cancellations. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy called for $50bn to modernise the system. Indra was selected in Jan 2026 for FAA upgrade plans alongside RTX and is the best-exposed European name.
Rightmove rose Friday on a Reuters report that activist Sachem Head is pushing it to consider a sale. The desk says it does not see why this should surprise and does not know why the stock rose.
Apple reportedly plans to unveil N50 smart glasses at WWDC in June 2027 with production before end-2026. The first generation lacks AR displays.
OpenAI launched ChatGPT Wallet, naming Adyen as a core payment service provider alongside Checkout.com and Stripe. The desk calls this a pleasant surprise.
SpaceX Flight 15 was a success in GIR's view. GIR keeps Buy on SPCX with a 12-month $245 price target unchanged.

GS Prime data: systematic L/S funds were up 3% for the week (best since Feb 2024, +17.7% YTD) and fundamental L/S up 1.1% (+9.7% YTD). The global book was net sold, 9 of 11 sectors were net sold led by Info Tech, Energy was the most net bought, and single stocks were net sold for 9 straight weeks.

Macro backdrop per Callahan: VIX at 20, 10-year at 5.13% following hot CPI, USD breaking out, oil in the high-$90s. NVDA shed about $500bn of market cap while AMD and AVGO together added about $500bn or more, so the week looked rotational.

Outlooks: Hatzius expects similar global growth in 2027 with downside risks (Middle East escalation, higher yields, AI capex disappointment) and early signs AI is weighing on hiring. Oppenheimer expects the equity bull market to continue. Sharon Bell has Europe underweight but sees AI diversification and a 5.5% FCF yield, and downgraded Banks to Neutral and Insurance and Energy to underweight.

market_movers.rationale: GIR keeps Buy and the 12-month $245 target after Flight 15 and Q3 results, with estimates unchanged.

Technoprobe: GIR cuts FY26 revenue estimate 3% and EBIT 9% on a c.€50mn 4Q headwind from the digital transformation project, and raises FY27-28 revenue c.2%. FY26-28 sales CAGR of c.40% still forecast.

Octave Intelligence 3Q26: revenue beat 3% and EBIT margin beat ~300bps, SaaS +18% YoY, but billings +1% and a miss. 4Q revenue guide below the Street; 2027 organic growth of about 3% a reasonable start.
Earnings Tuesday amid leadership uncertainty, possible Vera Rubin delay to 1H27 and heavy long-only supply.
GS expects cloud growth to accelerate to 53% with margins at 12.5%; earnings Thursday.
Desk flags 13x P/E ex-cash for 20%+ growth and a regulatory overhang resolved.

sector_views.rationale: Investors split on whether last week's move is a dead cat bounce or a bottom. Debate centres on Nvidia's funding capacity and China policy.
H-share Internet profit growth seen accelerating from -3% in 2026 to +18% in 2027, with AI and cloud fundamentals improving and positioning starting to turn.
Europe is underweight overall, but Bell sees AI diversification and a 5.5% FCF yield and recommends Tech, Retailers, Telecoms, Utilities, Defense and Renewables.

Alibaba (reports Thursday): GS forecasts cloud growth accelerating to 53% with cloud margin at 12.5%. Not yet printed.

tension_points.bull_case: Backlogs and TSMC allocations remain intact, NVDA trades at 11x forward earnings with RSI at its lowest since 2019, NDX snapped a four-week losing streak, and demand looks supply-constrained.
tension_points.bear_case: A more conservative Nvidia under new leadership could expose financing-dependent demand, Vera Rubin may slip to 1H27, China controls could tighten, and positioning data show new shorts and persistent long-only NVDA supply.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak Tuesday Nvidia print or guidance (revenue miss, gross margin below the 74% guide, or no reassurance on roughly 70% FY2028 growth) would support the dead-cat-bounce view.
